basis.independent_countercheck: Claude: TRAGFÄHIG MIT KORREKTUREN; no blocker before implementation

design_goal: Bound response generation before any new model contact while preserving the frozen 67-question semantic qualification scope.

candidate_transport.rationale: At the observed v1.5 decode range of roughly 1.5-1.76 tokens/s, a 1024-token generation ceiling bounds pure decoding to roughly 9.7-11.4 minutes instead of allowing generation to run until the 1800s transport timeout. This is a design bound only and has not been quality-qualified.

candidate_schema_cardinalities.assignment_cap_evidence: Frozen Human Gold has at most 3 expected-plus-optional assignments per case; comparison to the per-proposal cap is deliberately conservative and does not assert one proposal per SourceLocation.
candidate_schema_cardinalities.non_assignment_caps_evidence: Engineering safety bounds only. Frozen Human Gold does not positively establish required maxima for conflict refs, gap notes or uncertainty notes.
candidate_schema_cardinalities.rationale: Finite safety bounds are intentionally above the observed frozen-suite structural needs. They are candidate limits, not a semantic-contract release.

candidate_text_lengths.rationale: The independent countercheck identified unbounded free-text fields as a remaining route to excessively long structured output. These finite character limits are deliberately generous for the short frozen synthetic cases but are not claimed to be empirically quality-qualified.

context_strategy.reason: A PF/question prefilter could bias or narrow the qualification task and is therefore not introduced before separate model-free semantic equivalence work. The first candidate isolates output bounding from context reduction.
